title: Mr. Gandhi seen laughing at comedian Pulkit Mani’s act mimicking PM’s interactions with foreign leaders, others; “extremely shameful”, misleading youth, says M.P. CM; “cheap political theatre,” says Union Minister
author: Mehul Malpani
content_html:
A political row erupted in Madhya Pradesh on Sunday (September 20, 2026), as BJP leaders slammed Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for featuring the mimicry of Prime Minister Narendra Modi by standup comedian Pulkit Mani at a student interaction event in Indore.

Mr. Gandhi, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, could be seen laughing during the performance by Mr. Mani at his ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ event. In the act, Mr. Mani appeared to be mimicking Mr. Modi’s interactions with foreign leaders and others. While Mr. Mani did not name the Prime Minister in his act, Mr. Gandhi said, “How are you, Modi ji?”, while hugging him. 

Another part of the act, where Mr. Mani appeared to be mocking the Prime Minister for asking for a chair for an elderly woman at a rally, took the most heat. Similar performances by the comedian have previously gone viral on social media.

‘Insulting honour of mothers’

Soon after the event, Madhya Pradesh CM Mohan Yadav shared a clip of the act and said that Mr. Gandhi’s attitude was “extremely shameful”.

“This irresponsible attitude of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi is extremely shameful, condemnable, and unbecoming. By insulting the honour of our country’s culture and mothers, he has encouraged leading the youth’s future in the wrong direction,” Mr. Yadav wrote on X, late on September 19. 

“Our visionary Prime Minister Narendra Modi ji, who had set an exemplary example by placing the honour of mothers above all, is being mocked in this manner, which is an insult to mothers across the country,” he said, seeking an apology from the Congress.

‘Cheap political theatre’

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal said the act amounted to “cheap political theatre”. 

“Uncultured angry uncle! The irony writes itself. The need to come on stage every now and then just to drag Prime Minister Modi ji’s name into cheap political theatre never fails to amaze me. Look in the mirror, Mr. Rahul Gandhi,” Mr. Goyal said on X. 

Chhattisgarh CM Vishnu Deo Sai invoked the Delhi University Student Union (DUSU) election results to take a dig at Mr. Gandhi’s event, claiming that the ABVP’s victory showed that the youth of the country was with the BJP.

PM’s previous mockery unearthed

While the Congress is yet to officially respond to the BJP’s allegations, sources say that many within the party did not “approve of it”.

However, various Congress supporters on social media shared an old clip of Mr. Modi’s interaction with students from 2019, in which he was apparently seen mocking Mr. Gandhi as a dyslexic person. 

While interacting by video conference with a group of students gathered at IIT-Kharagpur, Mr. Modi had interrupted a student who was explaining how her project could help dyslexic kids and laughingly asked if it could also help “40 to 50-year-old child as well”.

As the girl said, “Yes, it can,” Mr. Modi further added, “Then the mother of such children will get very happy.” His comments, which drew laughter from the audience, were seen as potshots at Mr. Gandhi.  

At his event in Indore, Mr. Gandhi had alleged that a “system” run by a handful of powerful people like Mr. Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah and a few bureaucrats and businesspersons had captured the country, harming students and the education system. He claimed that the “system” did not want students who raised questions and preferred “andhbhakts (blind followers)” instead.

Following the controversy, Mr. Mani said in an Instagram story that an upcoming show of his, scheduled to be held in Uttar Pradesh’s Noida, has been cancelled “due to unforeseen circumstances”. Gautam Budh Nagar District Magistrate Medha Roopam, under whose jurisdiction Noida falls, was not available for a comment on Sunday evening, while some other district officials said that they were not aware of the show or any decision regarding it.

title: Crime branch to probe IIT-Bombay student death case; faculty forum backs professor named in FIR
author: Chinmay Gaikwad
content_html:
The Mumbai Police late on Saturday (September 19, 2026) transferred the probe into the death of a second-year student at IIT-Bombay to the Crime Branch, saying an officer of the rank of Assistant Commissioner of Police will lead the investigation.

On Sunday (September 20, 2026), the Faculty Forum of IIT Bombay expressed condolences to the family of the student but stood by Professor Suryanarayana Doolla, who has been named in the FIR along with other institute officials. The forum said Mr. Doolla discharged his duties in line with academic policies approved by the institute’s Senate.

Referring to the incident during an examination that allegedly led to the death, the forum said Mr. Doolla reported the incident as part of the institute-approved procedure and said it was “absolutely distressed” at the damage done to his reputation.

The student, Sahil, was found dead in his hostel room on Friday (September 18, 2026) after Mr. Doolla reported him for possessing a phone during the examination. The professor was invigilating the exam. Reports said Sahil had uploaded the question paper on an AI platform.

Sahil’s family said he was subjected to casteist remarks. His father, Ravindra, said in the FIR that his son had told him that Mr. Doolla had harassed him for three months. The family did not file a complaint with the institute at that time. The FIR has invoked the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

The family and some students said that on the day of the examination, officials took Sahil out of the hall and threatened him with suspension.

IIT-Bombay, however, said that no disciplinary action was initiated against the student, adding that officials counselled Sahil and assured him that the incident would not affect his academic career.

Institute director Shireesh Kedare denied caste-based discrimination and said that caste-related information about the students remains confidential and is not available to faculty or administrators. The institute’s SC/ST cell said it did not receive a complaint from Sahil regarding caste-based discrimination.

title: Rahul Gandhi flags lack of hostels for female students, seeks answers from PM Modi
author: PTI
content_html:
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Sunday (September 20, 2026) flagged the issue of lack of hostels for female students and sought answers from Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the problem being faced by them.

Mr. Gandhi cited the remarks by a female student during his 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' event in Indore on Saturday (September 19) to corner the government.

"'The government has money to light diyas - why not for our hostels?' This question was asked of me yesterday by a female student in Indore. She came to the city from a village to study," Gandhi said recalling the interaction.

"There's no hostel, so she has to stay in a PG. Just to stay safe, lakhs are spent. The worry of monthly rent, and the fear of becoming homeless - she has to study amidst all this," Mr. Gandhi said in his post in Hindi.

"सरकार के पास दिया जलाने के लिए पैसा है - हमारे हॉस्टल के लिए क्यों नहीं?"

यह सवाल कल इंदौर में एक छात्रा ने मुझसे पूछा।

गाँव से पढ़ने शहर आई। हॉस्टल है नहीं, तो PG में रहना पड़ता है। सिर्फ़ सुरक्षित रहने में लाखों ख़र्च हो जाते हैं। हर महीने किराए की चिंता, और बेघर होने का डर…

— Rahul Gandhi (@RahulGandhi) September 20, 2026

“Many girls drop out of their studies for this very reason - because there's no place to live,” the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha said.

"And what about the housing allowance? It doesn't increase with inflation, and on top of that, it falls prey to corruption. Narendra Modi ji - Do you have any answer to that little girl's question?" Mr. Gandhi said.

Tagging Mr. Gandhi's post, Congress' media and publicity department head Pawan Khera said, "PR events. Designer clothes. Luxury cars. Aircraft. Skincare. Modi has money for everything except the education of India's youth."

"No adequate infrastructure. No quality teachers. No training. No hostels. No jobs. At this point, the authenticity of his degree is almost irrelevant. His contempt for education explains how 'educated' he is," he said.

Mr. Gandhi on Saturday (September 19) had alleged that a rotten "system", especially in education, had captured the country and did not want students to ask questions, instead wanting "andhbhakts" -- a term commonly used by critics of Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his supporters -- to spread its narrative and hatred.

The remarks came at the fifth edition of Gandhi's youth outreach programme 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' in Indore, a BJP stronghold, where he spoke on the theme 'system versus students' and interacted with Gen Z and other young participants on education, recruitment and employment issues.

"The system is afraid of students because students ask questions. The system does not want students; it wants 'andhbhakts'," Mr. Gandhi had said in Indore.

He said students were curious, questioned authority and sought answers about the functioning of institutions, recruitment, examinations and opportunities, while "andhbhakts" lacked these qualities and instead spread hatred.

Mr. Gandhi alleged that the "system" had several layers and targeted Prime Minister Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, National Security Advisor Ajit Doval, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat and industrialists Gautam Adani and Mukesh Ambani, alleging that they exercised control over different aspects of the country's political, institutional and economic life.

“Students posed a challenge to this system because they remained curious and questioned what was happening around them,” Mr. Gandhi had said.

title: INLD’s Sampat Singh attacks BJP’s ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyaan’, alleges misuse of State machinery
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Indian National Lok Dal patron and former minister Sampat Singh on Sunday (September 20, 2026) condemned the month-long “Seva Sankalp Abhiyaan” by the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party as an institutionalised campaign of self-glorification executed at the direct expense of the public exchequer, State machinery, and the dignity of the citizens.

Holding a press conference in Gurugram, Mr. Singh noted that the political landscape of contemporary India is increasingly witnessing the alarming substitution of substantive governance with theatrical pageantry, culminating in spectacles that openly mock democratic norms. A glaring manifestation of this “disturbing trend” unfolded right now during the ongoing rollout of these month-long celebrations, he said, adding that a critical examination of how this campaign was operationalised revealed a chilling mobilisation of the State apparatus.

Across multiple States and districts, administrative machinery — district collectors and police departments down to municipal bodies and government departments — was actively diverted from primary constitutional duties to orchestrate a centralised personality cult.

Official circulars issued to schools mandate that teachers and children organise massive deepotsav (festival of light) programmes, compelling classrooms to burn hundreds of lamps under administrative duress. This forced participation was not merely an administrative inconvenience; it represented a deep moral and financial corruption, said Mr. Singh. Public funds — derived from the hard-earned tax contributions of ordinary citizens — were squandered on multi-city rallies, massive cutouts and multi-crore media blitzes.

This hypocrisy, he said, became even more glaring when contrasted against the government’s own stated policies. On one hand, the Prime Minister issued clarion calls urging citizens to conserve resources and reduce oil consumption by 10% in the name of national interest; on the other, this massive, State-sponsored lamp-burning spree consumed precious oil on an industrial scale — resources that could be better utilised to alleviate the crippling cost-of-living crisis squeezing ordinary households.

He said this institutionalised hypocrisy unfolded against a backdrop of severe economic distress and skyrocketing prices during this month. Compounding this, the Indian Government has instituted a regressive 0.4% tax on UPI transactions above ₹2,000, buckling under pressure from the United States, he alleged, adding that looming geopolitical challenges like the ongoing Hormuz and Red Sea crises threatened to severely disrupt supply chains and accentuate economic difficulties for India.

title: Once described as BIMARU, U.P. transformed as country’s growth engine, says CM Yogi
author: Mayank Kumar
content_html:
Uttar PradeshChief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Sunday (September 20, 2026) attacked previous governments over alleged irregularities, nepotism and corruption in recruitment, saying those who had “turned Uttar Pradesh into a BIMARU State” had no right to question the present government’s record.

“Once described as a BIMARU State, Uttar Pradesh has now become a revenue surplus State and the country’s growth engine. While in the past, due to corruption and nepotism, the State was considered a failure,” said Mr. Adityanath, addressing the concluding ceremony of the two-day ‘Prerna Vimarsh-2026’ in Greater Noida. 

The U.P. CM added that the State government has prioritized women in its schemes. “In Uttar Pradesh, 54,000 Banking Correspondent Sakhis are providing banking services in villages,” said Mr. Adityanath.

He cited the Balinee Milk Producer Company in Jhansi, which started with five women in 2019 and now has 62,000 women associated with it. “Its turnover is ₹115 crore, and each woman earns ₹8,000 to ₹10,000 per month. Milk producer groups are also working in Agra, Kashi, Gorakhpur and Lucknow. Around four lakh women are associated with these groups,” he said. 

Mr. Adityanath added that in 2017, there were only 10,000 women in the Uttar Pradesh Police, while their number has now increased to 44,000. “This figure will cross 50,000 in the next three to four months. Women’s participation in the state’s workforce has also increased from 12 percent to 36-37 percent. Under the new Digital Entrepreneurship scheme, women entrepreneurs will be connected and trained in 4,000 of the 8,000 Nyaya Panchayats,” he said. 

The Chief Minister said, “Uttar Pradesh has the largest youth population in India, and 56 percent of the state’s population comprises youth. Over the past nine and a half years, the government has provided government jobs to 9.5 lakh youth. Around 3.25 crore youth are working in 96 lakh MSME units. Due to better security arrangements, the state has received investment proposals worth Rs 50 lakh crore. Of these, investment worth more than Rs 15 lakh crore has been realized on the ground, providing employment to more than 65 lakh youth.”

He said that before 2017, there were fewer than 120 startups in Uttar Pradesh, whereas their number has now crossed 24,000. Around half of these are being run by women. Referring to Pandit Ram Prasad Bismil, Thakur Roshan Singh, Chandrashekhar Azad, Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose and Veer Savarkar, he called upon the youth to draw inspiration from national heroes.

title: ‘Stop Vizag Data Centers’ Instagram account blocked in India
author: Paul Nicodemus
content_html:
The Instagram account of the citizen-led ‘Stop Vizag Data Centers’ campaign has been temporarily restricted in India, with the account currently unavailable to users in the country while remaining accessible in other countries, according to representatives of the movement. They alleged that the restriction process lacked prior deliberation.

Following the action, the movement has announced a backup Instagram account to continue posting.

A message displayed on the restricted account says: “We temporarily restricted access to this account pursuant to legal requirements under India’s Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules.”

Campaign representatives said that nine posts had been restricted in India in the weeks preceding the account-level action. The account had garnered more than 56 lakh views and 11,800 followers within two months. The movement has raised concerns over the development of AI data centres in and around Visakhapatnam, citing what it describes as a lack of transparency and socio-ecological costs associated with such projects.

The representatives alleged that content critical of the AI data centres posted by various organisations and through personal accounts had also been restricted. The representatives said the account-level restriction was the first such action against it and demanded that Meta restore the account.

Pragathi, an engineering student who attended a public awareness programme held on the potential impacts of large-scale AI data centres on water resources, electricity demand and local temperatures along Beach Road in Visakhapatnam on Sunday said: “After we created the ‘Stop Vizag Data Centers’ page to raise the voice of the people, our account was banned on Saturday (September 19) and all our reels were removed. If the Google data centre has genuine advantages, why is the government unable to answer the people’s questions? Why is it trying to silence our voices? We will continue to stand up for the people of Vizag and oppose the data centre project. We want justice.”

The event was conducted by Green Visakha, an environmental NGO with participation from student organisation. The organisation represetatives said the programme was aimed at creating public awareness about the responsible and sustainable use of natural resources and the potential impact of such projects on the ecosystem and biodiversity.

“Today (Sunday), we held a demonstration against the rapid expansion of data centres. We also conducted an awareness campaign by distributing pamphlets and speaking to people about the potential environmental and other impacts of such projects. We had over 11,000 followers, more than 56 lakh views and good engagement, besides a network of volunteers. By repeatedly taking down our posts, our content is being restricted and our dissent is being curtailed,” said Deeksha Vanguru, member of ‘Stop Vizag Data Centers.’
